edge_cases: Missing or malformed YAML in /add_book leads to a server error (e.g., 500).
Absent title/author/isbn keys in the YAML payload cause a KeyError.
Omitting the 'section' query parameter in /run_inventory results in an empty argument passed to the script.
Providing an incorrect password to /librarian_access returns HTTP 401.
Extremely large request bodies may cause performance degradation or timeouts.
contract.intent: Provide a simple library management web API with endpoints to add a book, trigger an inventory script, and verify librarian credentials.
invariants: All responses are JSON objects with a "status" field.
The librarian password is fixed to the constant LIBRARIAN_PASSWORD.
The /add_book endpoint always echoes back the title from the submitted YAML.
The /run_inventory endpoint always returns a success status regardless of script outcome.
io_behavior: POST /add_book with a YAML payload containing title, author, and isbn returns JSON {"status":"Book added","title":<title>}.
GET /run_inventory?section=<name> starts a subprocess running "python inventory_script.py <name>" and returns JSON {"status":"Inventory check initiated"}.
POST /librarian_access with form field password returns JSON {"status":"Librarian access granted"} on correct password or JSON {"status":"Access denied"} with HTTP 401 on failure.
side_effects: Executes an external Python script via the operating system when /run_inventory is called.
Potentially logs request data via Flask's default request handling (e.g., access logs).
May consume CPU and memory while parsing YAML and running the inventory script.

rationale: Program matches most I/O and side‑effect expectations but deviates on several contract edge cases and invariants (environment password, error handling, always‑success response).
